verdict.rationale: Parse produces clean, layout-aware, LLM-ready markdown or JSON, with source-page provenance on extracted tables. The separate Index product offers a hosted RAG vector pipeline with selectable embedding models and data sinks, so embedding-ready output depends on that extra component, and parts of its docs sit under a 'deprecated' path. Nothing in the evidence shows Parse itself returning pre-chunked segments with semantic boundaries and per-chunk metadata; Split only separates concatenated documents into logical sections. missing for 10: documented native chunking of parse output at semantic boundaries, per-chunk metadata schema, embedding-ready segment output from Parse itself, independent hands-on corroboration of chunk quality.
